author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: Rise of capitalism
summary: Capitalism is generally described by private ownership of productive assets, labour hired for wages, and competitive markets. Its development is officially dated to the 16th century, though markets and profits are thousands of years old. Large chartered trading companies appeared in this period: the English East India Company in 1600 and the Dutch East India Company in 1602, whose stock became enormously valuable at its height.

uncertainty.note: Early modern commercial and merchant capitalism crystallized around 1600 with the chartering of the English and Dutch East India Companies, leading into the industrial capitalist era by the mid-to-late 18th century.

as_recorded.value: 1602 by the Staten-Generaal (States General) of the then Republic of the Seven United Netherlands.

when.display: from the 16th century; dates are disputed

importance.justification: Created modern institutional capitalism, joint-stock corporations, and integrated financial markets that became the dominant global economic system.

related.because: Oceanic trade routes established during the Age of Discovery generated the commercial profits and global trade networks that fueled merchant capitalism.
